title: TIAA’s AI flags a suspected scam involving a 76-year-old’s retirement savings, and staff stop the money from moving
summary: TIAA’s CEO said that an AI flag, staff intervention, and contact with a participant’s daughter protected retirement savings of more than $3 million.
account: TIAA CEO Thasunda Brown Duckett told Fortune that an AI alert helped staff stop a scam involving a 76-year-old participant’s retirement savings. A portfolio manager referred the concern to the fraud team, which spent hours with the participant and contacted his daughter. Duckett said that the money did not move. The interview describes retirement holdings above $3 million, but does not itemize an attempted transfer. The original episode was released on June 17, 2026, with its transcript published five days later. No participant statement, transaction record, or separate investigation is supplied.
purpose: The unnamed AI tool flagged suspected fraud for human review. Staff investigation and contact with the participant’s family were necessary to stop the money from moving.
system: Unnamed TIAA AI tool used to flag suspected fraud for human review
deployer: TIAA (Teachers Insurance and Annuity Association of America)
domain: Financial services / retirement accounts / fraud prevention
segment: Retirement savings provider for educators, healthcare workers and public servants

ratings.reason: The CEO describes a 76-year-old retaining retirement savings of more than $3 million after a suspected scam was interrupted. The participant is unnamed, and no transaction record or independent account establishes the amount at risk or the counterfactual loss.
The CEO describes a successful fraud intervention by TIAA staff. The source does not quantify TIAA’s own avoided cost or the cost of the intervention.

ai_role.statement: Duckett attributes the initial flag to AI and the successful intervention to a portfolio manager, the fraud team, and the participant’s daughter. The transcript does not establish the model’s design, the requested transfer amount, or what would have happened without its flag.

evidence.citation: Thasunda Brown Duckett, interview by Alyson Shontell, Fortune 500: Titans and Disruptors of Industry, released June 17, 2026; lightly edited transcript published by Fortune Editors on June 22, 2026, “How TIAA is approaching AI—and whether it threatens the retirement market.”
